chapter: Clubs, publishers, unions and life in Denver
title: Fletcher enjoying conducting with the baton and his Honeysuckle Rose feature
summary: Later Fletcher loved waving the baton and cutting steps in front of the band, and his men knew the tunes called for him to perform.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Sure. Do you think that Fletcher himself considered himself as a -- what did he enjoy most doing? Playing piano, arranging, being a bandleader, or do you think there was any real differentiation?

Well, it was a combination of all of those, you know, like in arranging. If he had a tune to arrange, and it was a standard or something he knew real well, well, it was no sweat. He enjoyed doing it, and I think he -- sometimes he would turn out terrific arrangements, you know, and, of course, I think in the later years I actually believe Fletcher got a kick out of conducting his band because he used to like to playing with the baton, you know. He didn't go to school to learn to wave it or and one of those things. He had his own style, you know, and it was probably awkward to the thorough baton wielder (unintelligible), but he could do some things with it, and he got results.

And he learned how to cover -- to cut, rather, a few little steps in front of the band, and, man, you looked forward to that. And he liked that, you know. And, oh, man, sometimes the band would get swinging, and, boy, that chorus, outcourse, the band was just -- you could tell he'd feel it. Oh, his shoulders would go up, and he'd get to twisting, and the guys would say, "Yeah, he feels that tonight, you know, one of those things, you know, and he'd like this. He began
to look forward to that, and we could tell by certain tunes at certain time of the night that he would call, he was calling them for Fletcher.

To perform, (Unintelligible), you know. The guys got so they knew this, man, and say, "Okay, Smack, you're on," you know. And he would cut up -- especially if he had a receptive audience, you know. Oh, he'd love this. And, of course, like maybe on Honeysuckle Rose, the arrangement that features him on the piano. He would look forward to doing that tune, and he would like it. And he always liked to play tunes that moved pretty fast because he was at his best then, you know, because of the execution.
